From: Maria Alvarez <maria@aurelia.ai>

Cc: ops@aurelia.ai
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity needs for Q3 pilot (US/EU/APAC)

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Aurelia is greenlit to run a 3-region pilot with us for Q3 (60-day pilot, then conversion discussion). High level ask below — please treat numbers as expected consumption windows for now:

- US (primary): sustained conversational traffic ~120M tokens/month, peak windows up to 250 concurrent requests (avg 80 tokens/request), target p95 latency < 220ms
- EU (secondary, latency-sensitive): 35M tokens/month, peaks ~80 concurrent, p95 < 250ms and data-residency in Frankfurt
- APAC (pilot footprint): 8M tokens/month with two short spikes per day (morning/evening) up to 40 concurrent; p95 < 300ms

Model preferences are the Redwood-verified family (causal LLMs). We prefer to start with an 8-bit quantized variant for EU to save cost if latency allows. For US we are okay with an H100-backed offering for better throughput.

Timeline: pilot go-live per region staggered — US target 2027-07-01, EU 2027-07-15, APAC 2027-08-01. Aurelia expects to sign an SOW this week; can you provide a regionized activation slate (node counts, pre-warm plan, canary strategy) and an indicative cost delta between reserved vs committed burst model?

Attached is a short forecast (aurelia_q3_forecast.xlsx) and latency targets (aurelia_latency_targets.pdf).

Thanks,
Maria
Head of Platform
Aurelia Systems

Maria — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. Looping in Irene and Rishi to stamp operational and commercial constraints. Quick proposal here for the activation slate; we’ll follow up with a line-item cost after we validate instance availability.

High-level activation slate (first pass):
- US (sustained): 8x H100-80GB nodes dedicated (sustained requests), 2x warm-standby H100 nodes for fast failover and canary -> canary rollout 10% traffic for first 72 hours. Pre-warm to be scheduled 48 hours before go-live.
- EU (Frankfurt): 6x A100-80GB nodes (mix of quantized variants). Apply aggressive KV prefix caching and batching to meet p95 goals; plan one canary node (A100) with geo-routing via FR region.
- APAC (Singapore pilot): 3x L4 (cost-optimized inference nodes) + access to shared burst pool (region-tilt) for the two daily spikes. Pre-warm function to run 30 minutes before expected spikes.

Operational notes:
- We assume ~20% effective reduction in token load from prefix caching + batching in-proxy; will re-run calculations if Aurelia's payloads have larger prompts.
- Provisioning lead time: 6-8 weeks for Dedicated fleet adjustments; if Aurelia signs SOW this week we can aim for US go-live on 2027-07-01 but EU may slip by 1 week if procurement is delayed.
- Fallback: if region capacity constrained, our smart routing can spill to compatible variants in a neighboring region (with latency increase) — requires Aurelia sign-off.

Can Irene/Rishi confirm node-class availability and rough cost delta (reserved vs burst) and Marissa to nudge procurement if we need expedited procurement?

Thanks,
Dylan
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Dylan — quick capacity math and a couple of clarifying asks (quoting Maria for context below).

On Tue, 4 May 2027 09:12, Maria Alvarez <maria@aurelia.ai> wrote:
> - US: 120M tokens/month; peaks 250 concurrent; avg 80 tokens/request
> - EU: 35M tokens/month; peaks 80 concurrent

Assumptions used:
- Model emits ~80 tokens/request avg (you listed that), typical batch factor 1.8 in steady-state, 2.5 in peak bursts.
- H100 sustained concurrency per node (realistic with Redwood runtime and batching) ~28 concurrent effective requests at target latency for 80-token avg. That equates to ~2,240 tokens/s per H100 node sustained.

Preliminary node counts (after 20% reduction from caching/batching):
- US: 120M tokens/month -> ~46,300 tokens/hour -> ~13 tokens/s avg -> factoring peaks and p95 SLO we recommend 7-8 H100 nodes (aligns with Dylan).
- EU: 35M tokens/month -> recommend 5-6 A100 nodes (quantized) with one reserved for canary + one standby for failover.
- APAC: 8M tokens/month -> 2-3 L4 nodes with policy-managed burst to shared pool.

Costs: rough multiplier
- Reserved (monthly committed) ~0.72x of on-demand for these node classes
- Committed-burst (pay for baseline + burst) is easier to sign quickly but has higher unit cost ~0.9x on-demand for sustained months; overall pilot economics favor reserved if Aurelia commits to >60% of forecast.

Action items for Aurelia:
1) Share token-size distribution (are there many 300+ token replies?)
2) Confirm tolerance for cross-region failover (we need explicit permission to route EU->US during brief overloads)

I’ll slot this into the region activation runbook and provide a draft SOW appendix.

- Irene
Director, Capacity & Operations
Redwood Inference

Team — commercial guardrails we should surface to Aurelia and embed in the SOW:

1) Tranche activation gates:
- Gate A (Sign + Initial payment): provision baseline reserved capacity in US (minimum 4 H100 nodes live within 7 business days).
- Gate B (Usage thresholds hit in pilot month 1): commit to remaining nodes per region. Trigger defined as 60% of forecasted sustained tokens for 10 consecutive days.

2) Minimum monthly commit per region (for reserved pricing):
- US: min 70M tokens/month equivalent (maps to 4 H100 reserved baseline)
- EU: min 20M tokens/month equivalent
- APAC: min 5M tokens/month equivalent

3) Fallback and credits:
- If we spill to cross-region or shared pool > 8% of requests in a billing period, Aurelia gets a service credit tier.

4) Fractional reserved nodes: we can offer a fractional-reserve model (e.g., 0.5 node equivalents) to smooth costs — useful for APAC spikes.

Marissa — can you confirm procurement flow/time to invoice and whether Finance can issue a 30-day pilot invoice plan? I’ll draft SOW language for the tranche triggers and credit table.

- Rishi
Head of Deal Structuring
Redwood Inference
